heading: Simple mappings can make representations interchangeable across models
definition: one model's representations can be mapped onto another's with little loss, by a simple (often linear) map, by stitching layers, through relative representations, or even without paired data.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce successful mappings and stitches—connections joining parts of different models—for selected model pairs and tasks, but general interchangeability remains contested. Mappings that predict activations well can fail when used to replace one model's representations with another's, and alignment without paired examples gives mixed results.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: C for general functional interchangeability, with R2 for selected mappings and stitches; 1-10B: C broadly, with R2 in compatible pairs; 10-100B: C for general linear interchangeability, with R2 for selected within-family cache transfers. >100B: ?; counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size has no >100B entry. Toy evidence is not separately bucketed.
suggested_status.reason: C applies to the unqualified V4 wording; narrower successes reach R2. Task-trained affine stitches preserve selected ResNet-20 and Inception tasks (arXiv:2110.14633#r1, arXiv:2110.14633#r3), while Pythia-160M→410M frozen replacement substantially reduces answer containment despite strong offline fit (arXiv:2606.03280#r1, arXiv:2606.03280#r2, arXiv:2606.03280#r7). Cross-family ridge screening finds incompatible language-model pairs (arXiv:2608.09521#r35, arXiv:2608.09521#r36). Within-family cache maps succeed on selected benchmarks but fail for Ministral→14B pairs (arXiv:2608.03893#r01, arXiv:2608.03893#r21, arXiv:2608.03893#r24). Counts: versions.V4.verdicts.supports.studies=112, versions.V4.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=137, and versions.V4.verdicts.challenges.studies=25; these categories overlap.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched independent tests of failed pairs could distinguish map-fitting failures from unavailable transferable information. Broadening the status would require low-loss frozen-receiver substitution across heterogeneous pairs, tasks and held-out distributions, including unpaired full-sequence generation. Explicitly identified models above 100B remain uncovered by the size counts.

source.title: Convergent Learning: Do different neural networks learn the same representations?
source.authors: Yi-Xuan Li; J. Yosinski; J. Clune; Hod Lipson; J. Hopcroft

original_result.setup: Li et al. fitted linear maps with L1 penalties, which encourage few nonzero weights, to predict one network's activations (Net2) from the corresponding layers of another (Net1).
original_result.result: With L1 decay 10^-4, average prediction error after 4,500 iterations was 0.162 at conv1 and 0.439 at conv5. These measurements tested activation prediction; they did not establish preservation of downstream behavior.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

wording_issues.issue: Specify the preserved property, metric and reference. Relative FastText↔Word2Vec MRR is 0.94–0.98 while neighborhood Jaccard is 0.34–0.39. IRP reconstruction cosine is 0.97; mean cosine between distinct English embeddings in the absolute target space is 0.93 ± 0.05. Screen-retained LM ridge maps explain only 0.35–0.44 of variance despite strong retrieval. Pathology shared-space Recall@1 is 0.997; native cross-model translation on TCGA at 20×, 224 px gives Recall@1 0.470 versus self round-trip 0.807.

Representation fit, retrained-readout performance and frozen-receiver substitution need separate descriptions. Pythia-160M layer 8→410M layer 16 has normalized R² 0.882773, yet replacement lowers answer containment from 0.0884 to 0.0025. Causal-decoder MLP retrieval reaches 45–50%, while injection into Mistral gives 0.0% versus 3.3% control. Protein projection R² is high but functional patching is partial. In the toy XL→XS setup, frozen-readout retention is partial at default α=1 (50.2%), scaled α=1 (67.5%) and α=10 (66.3%), but reversed at α=100 (−33.1%); retrained probes can preserve information despite frozen-readout failure.

Transformation constraints, fitting objective and interface training are consequential. On IJB-C at FAR 0.01, general linear maps give mean verification TAR 0.95 versus rotation-only 0.91 and unmapped 0.96; this measures downstream preservation. Direct least-squares or sparse matching can fail where task-trained affine stitches succeed. Figure 8's illustrative sparse direct match has relative accuracy 11.60% at sparsity 0.974, versus 94.64% at sparsity 0.000. Nonlinear MLP cache maps restore 92–96% HellaSwag retention for selected linear-failure pairs. Successful diffusion→reward-model stitching uses a nonlinear residual MLP and finetunes the receiving suffix; a frozen, purely linear retrieval comparison is untested, so necessity of these adaptations is not established.

State the cut, objective, direction and whether the receiver is adapted. Task-trained Small ResNet stitches reach near 90% accuracy in the lower-left layer region; the MSE sanity comparisons do not establish receiver hacking. Within-family LM A→B→A round trips increase cross-entropy by <1% for the tested GPT2, Pythia and Gemma pairs; B→A→B increases it by 1.4%, 4.7% and 13%, respectively. Direct stitches increase cross-entropy by 8.3–39%. Invariance-aware tests expose incompatibility concealed by standard stitching. VIST3A reports performance only after downstream finetuning, leaving the linear stitch's standalone cost unknown.

Relative coordinates require qualified anchor, normalization and task conditions. PARAM-WIP gives Tiny→GPT2 R@1 93.44 ± 0.34%, versus Random-Cosine 0.50 ± 0.18%, with no stated chance baseline. For MNIST AE4 input embeddings decoded by a relative decoder trained on AE1 embeddings, latent dimension and anchor count 64, PARAM Multi/WIP reconstruction succeeds while Random-Cosine reconstruction almost entirely fails. Vanilla English/French RoBERTa stitching has substantial losses that robust normalization reduces. Lorenz-63 cross-family relative stitching is worse than absolute stitching. Deception-probe transfer weakens across elicitation formats. Under filler padding, Phi-3 pairings collapse or invert; Qwen→Phi-3 falls from prose-reported unpadded AUC 0.96 to near 0, a reversed transfer whose causal interpretation is limited by the unresolved padding artifact.

Qualify this by model pair, recoverable geometry, optimization and remaining supervision. GeoWarP succeeds for selected pairs but stays near chance on its low-alignment scientific pairs: Rosetta Cell Painting–L1000 FOSCTTM is 0.48 ± 0.10; DESI galaxy–spectrum is 0.57 ± 0.00 at Table 12's precision. CoSAE with both translation and concept-consistency objectives distributional gives translation R² 0.0000 and Mtr 0.1428, an absent transfer result. JEPA pair-free Flickr retrieval varies strongly with encoder choice and across runs. LFM's geodesic and cosine descriptors use 10 correspondences and perform best; label descriptors are weakly supervised, while HKS and WKS are fully unsupervised. Exact Figure 8 score-to-descriptor assignments are unverified in the extracted text.

Specify which information or coordinates are transferred. Qwen3 projector cosine is 93.7–95.0% over selected low-rank directions but 77.0% at the paper's stated full rank, without reported held-out map evaluation. Concept-conditioned ridge maps test binary information in PCA-50 space; random-label affine accuracy is the fraction 0.504 ± 0.009. These transfer accuracies do not determine geometric completeness or its causes. Shared-head transplantation concerns selected heads in shared-base LoRA fine-tunes.

A successful directed map does not establish mutual interchangeability. Ventriloquist Qwen14B→Mistral-Nemo generation scores 1.86 versus 4.13 in reverse. Jet-tagger stitching depends strongly on direction and depth. A successful forward backdoor map can have a failing pseudo-inverse. Vision stitching also reports forward/reverse asymmetry over depth-mixed pairs.

State the fitting and evaluation distributions. Cross-trait affine classification is 0.707 versus 0.999 for the same trait. Prose-fitted shared-space retrieval is partial on unfamiliar inputs: unseen-category retrieval is 0.29–0.36 against chance 0.10 in pools of ten; mathematical expressions score 0.30 in text versus 0.29 in Figure 6a, and symbolic notation 0.24 versus 0.23. A trained LM interface has in-distribution R@1 at least 99.6% but behavioral-OOD R@1 60.8–78.7%. Semantic→collaborative MLP-2 mapping nearly reproduces seen training items, with R² 0.977, but unseen-item R² is −0.487.

method_sensitivity.factor: Layer, receiving cut and substitution route
method_sensitivity.what: SD3.5-M→CLIP MSCOCO directional-mean R@1 is 46.9–49.7% at receiving cuts j≤4 after Stage-2 training, versus 0.1–5.0% at j=16/22. Clean CLIP ViT-L/14 reports separate image-to-text/text-to-image R@1 values of 57.90%/37.09%. Successful stitches use a nonlinear residual MLP and suffix finetuning; their necessity is untested. ParT→Lund-ParT retained background rejection changes from 0.202 at depth 1 to 0.913 at depth 5. Moving the AFHQ BigGAN receiving target shallower raises Layer3 reconstruction cosine from 0.316 to 0.724. Selected within-family, same-data LM A→B→A round trips can be near-lossless while direct stitches cost +8% to +39% cross-entropy.

method_sensitivity.factor: Map constraints, capacity and fitting objective
method_sensitivity.what: IJB-C general linear mapping gives mean TAR 0.95 versus rotation-only 0.91 in 1:1 verification at FAR 0.01; this measures downstream preservation rather than representational completeness. Task-trained ResNet-20 stitches preserve accuracy where direct least-squares maps can fail. Illustrative sparse direct-matching relative accuracies are 94.64% at sparsity 0.000, 63.64% at 0.798 and 11.60% at 0.974; the last example is outside approximately 80–90% sparsity. Pythia-1.4B→410M full ridge gives held-out R² 0.844 versus rotation-plus-scale 0.717. Under driving sensor shift, convolutional stitching reaches Driving Score 91.19 versus linear 43.79. Increased map flexibility therefore has condition-dependent benefits.

method_sensitivity.factor: Anchors, paired supervision and unsupervised optimization
method_sensitivity.what: For TinyLlama→GPT-2, PARAM-WIP R@1 is 93.44 ± 0.34% versus Random-Cosine 0.50 ± 0.18%; no chance baseline is stated. PARAM weakens with very small support sets, with marginal gains beyond approximately 5,000–10,000 parallel points. Flickr30k DINOv2–MiniLM Procrustes/relative R@1 is 2.1–3.4% with 20 anchors; with 500, Procrustes reaches 55.5% and relative representations 26.6%. CoSAE mixed training with 1-in-100 pairs gives Mtr 0.7317 and translation R² 0.4224, indicating partial recovery. With both alignment objectives distributional, Mtr is 0.1428 and translation R² 0.0000. mini-vec2vec gtr↔gte has frequent suboptimal convergence at c=20; tuned c=30 gives top-1 0.98 ± 0.00 in each direction over 3 runs.

method_sensitivity.factor: Alignment corpus, encoder objective and evaluation distribution
method_sensitivity.what: Concept-rich versus retrieval-focused DINOv2-Large/All-Roberta-Large-v1 projector training gives ImageNet accuracy 76.12% versus 54.17%, but Flickr image-to-text retrieval 52.70% versus 85.30%. The concept-rich classification and retrieval-focused retrieval results preserve their respective measures well; the losses concern the other task. Prose-fitted GPA retrieval on shifted code/multilingual content is 0.29–0.36 against chance 0.10; matched five-fold retrieval increases from 0.45 to 0.84 when fitting includes code and multilingual probes. Removing concepts from small ViT-B/16 + GPT2-small adapter training sharply reduces detection of those concepts. Pair-free Flickr JEPA retrieval is 16.4% ± 10.4% for good-view encoders versus at most 0.3% for other text encoders.

Pythia-160M→410M mapped activations have cosine 0.973526, yet replacement reduces answer containment from 0.0884 to 0.0025. Pathology GCCA shared-space Recall@1 0.997 coexists with native-space translation Recall@1 0.470; the latter is for TCGA, 20×, 224 px, versus self round-trip 0.807. A held-out Qwen coder sender has cache cosine 0.9933 without significant controlled transfer. Diffusion→DINOv3 mapping loses only 0.00–0.23 percentage points of attribute accuracy despite mapped cosine 0.54–0.57. These metrics test different preservation properties.

method_sensitivity.factor: Representation preprocessing, bridge rank and operator masking
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen3-1.7B→4B projected cosine peaks at 95.0% at rank 8 but falls to 77.0% at full rank 2048; held-out map evaluation is not reported. Adding rotation to transport raises DINOv2-Small↔ViT-MAE-Base held-out activation-reconstruction correlation from 0.289 to 0.600; downstream interchangeability is untested. Sparse SAE transport explains 0.85 only when the whole target operator is evaluated on the source coactive block, versus 0.47 for the genuinely masked target. Robust normalization substantially improves English/French RoBERTa transfer over vanilla relative coordinates.

method_sensitivity.factor: Model capability, training conditions and reference coverage
method_sensitivity.what: Weak CNN/face models map less reliably, and smaller IJB-C fitting sets degrade compatibility. Coarse-label or partially noisy-label CIFAR-10 networks remain compatible mainly in their first half; a fully noisy-label network fails. Sparse-atlas attachment depends on reference-panel coverage: held-out Qwen incurs cross-entropy change +1.04 nats versus its in-panel +0.05 nats.

method_sensitivity.factor: Steering layer, intervention strength, concept and map
method_sensitivity.what: Cross-family OLS steering uses manually selected layers and β; excessive β can garble output. Gemma myopic-reward steering has transferred-versus-native correlation 0.728 ± 0.344, weaker than its successful tasks. Atlas Procrustes retrieval reaches MRR 0.97 while unconstrained regression is near random at 0.02–0.03 in its reported fitting setting. The near-random OLS condition is absent V4 transfer and observed method dependence under V6; it does not establish failure for every OLS fitting regime.

method_sensitivity.factor: Geometry criterion, task structure and optimization assumptions
method_sensitivity.what: Interatomic-potential global Procrustes agreement exceeds 0.86 while local mKNN remains below 0.38; local fidelity is incomplete despite strong global agreement. Held-out orthogonal VLM displacement maps have mean normalized residual 1.049 against mean-prediction baseline 1.0, but Denoising/Motion Deblurring reach 0.74/0.83. The deep-linear exact scaling/rotation guarantee depends on gradient-balance assumptions and does not hold universally in its weight-balance regime. Failure of that special guarantee does not establish failure of another simple linear map.

method_sensitivity.factor: Donor–target direction, source capacity, benchmark and environment
method_sensitivity.what: Ventriloquist Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct→Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 generation scores 1.86 versus 4.13 in reverse on its 1–10 judge. Llama-3.1 8B→70B linear KV transfer retains 18.2% on GSM8K, 90.9% on ARC-C and 94.4% on HellaSwag. Medical→Finance shared-head recovery is 0.59 versus Finance→Medical 1.10. At epoch 10, Wall MAE→DINOv2-S world-model stitching succeeds at 0.02 against endpoint success rates MAE 0.56 and DINOv2-S 0.90, contrasting with selected successful PointMaze interfaces.
